title: Weak nuclear force (দুর্বল নিউক্লীয় বল)
placement: Book page 68, topic 3.2.3: দুর্বল নিউক্লীয় বল (Weak Nuclear Force), next to that paragraph.
description: Interactive 3D figure for the weak nuclear force (দুর্বল নিউক্লীয় বল), book page 68, topic 3.2.3. A radioactive nucleus (তেজস্ক্রিয় নিউক্লিয়াস: 6 protons, 8 neutrons, like carbon-14): the student taps it (or presses β রশ্মি দেখো) and sees, slowed down a great deal, the weak force act at a point inside one neutron, the neutron turn into a proton (marked “নিউট্রন → প্রোটন”) as an electron, the beta (β) ray, shoots out in a straight line and stops inside the view; the panel counts protons 6 → 7 and neutrons 8 → 7. A zoom with three stops shows how short the force's reach is: the whole atom (about 10⁻¹⁰ m, held by the electromagnetic force), the nucleus, and, slowly, a thousand times closer inside that neutron, the weak force's reach, a sphere of 10⁻¹⁸ m (like a grain of sand beside a football); a scale bar follows the zoom and says what part of a neutron it is. The panel keeps the four fundamental forces in order, weakest first, with their ranges, and the book's sentence on strength (weaker than the electromagnetic force by about a trillion times, far stronger than gravity). Test tab: 5 questions (which force causes the β ray, always first; what the β ray is or how many protons are left; the force's range or a comparison with gravity; how many times smaller the reach is than a neutron; its strength among the four forces). The scene is drawn in femtometres; the GLB (the nucleus) is written with 1 fm as 1 cm (10¹³ times life size), as in strong-nuclear-force. Phone-first, Bangla.
